name: Blue/Blue Belly (2014 refresh)
description: White fuselage with a navy belly from the nose to behind the wing; 'jetBlue' in large navy lower case over the forward windows; navy engines with 'jetblue.com' in white; the fin carries one of JetBlue's tail designs (Bubbles, Mosaic, Dots, Harbor, Highrise, Pinstripes and others, in shades of blue) with 'jetBlue' in white on it.

logos.description: One of JetBlue's tail designs filling the fin: overlapping discs (Bubbles), squares (Mosaic), dots, stripes or skylines, in light, mid and dark blues. Each aircraft carries one; the fin title is the same on all.
A small US flag ahead of the registration over the rear windows.

titles.style: The jetBlue wordmark: heavy rounded geometric sans, lower case with a capital B, navy, over the forward windows behind the door; a small ® after it.
The wordmark in white across the middle of the fin.
Bold rounded lower case along the cowling's side.

notes: Drawn from the A321neo N2017J (Dec 2025). The fin is the airline's family of tail designs: the areas give only a rough idea of the Bubbles design seen on this aircraft. Each aircraft also has a name ('Crème Bluelée' here) under the cockpit, not drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 for the A320 (JetBlue's commonest type): the title measured on N2017J in metres (starts 1.5 m behind the forward door's middle, 6.8 m long, cap height 1.57 m, its baseline about 0.47 m under the windows' bottom; lowercase 0.76 of the capitals) and placed on the A320's outline, checked against N627JB (A320); 'jetblue.com' on the A320's nacelle runs x 0.43-0.79 (N627JB, N615JB; on the A321neo's it is further forward, 0.14-0.64). The fin title is larger than first drawn: baseline at 0.18 of the fin, cap 0.16, x 0.31-0.84 of the chord on both types. On the A321 the title covers a smaller share (x 0.137-0.290).
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximate standard (a few colors from memory). The 2014 refresh added the navy belly and 'jetblue.com' engines to the 2000 white-and-blue tail design scheme.
